gloss: to trample down; to default on

definitions.gloss: to trample down, to knock down by stepping on
definitions.explanation: To knock something or someone down by stepping on or trampling.

definitions.gloss: to default on, to skip out on (payment)
definitions.explanation: To fail to pay a debt or bill, especially with no intention of paying. Often implies running away from the obligation.

examples.japanese: {花壇|かだん}の{花|はな}を{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}してしまった。
examples.english: I accidentally trampled down the flowers in the flower bed.

examples.japanese: {風|かぜ}で{稲|いね}が{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}されたようになっている。
examples.english: The rice plants look like they've been trampled down by the wind.

examples.japanese: {群衆|ぐんしゅう}が{柵|さく}を{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}して{会場|かいじょう}に{入|はい}った。
examples.english: The crowd trampled down the fences and entered the venue.

examples.japanese: {借金|しゃっきん}を{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}して{逃|に}げた。
examples.english: He skipped out on his debt and ran away.

examples.japanese: {飲食代|いんしょくだい}を{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}す{客|きゃく}がいる。
examples.english: There are customers who skip out on their restaurant bills.

examples.japanese: {家賃|やちん}を{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}されて{困|こま}っている。
examples.english: I'm in trouble because someone defaulted on rent payments.

notes:
COMPOUND VERB: {踏|ふ}む (to step on) + {倒|たお}す (to knock down) = to step on and knock down

TRANSITIVITY: Transitive. Takes を to mark what is being trampled or the debt being defaulted.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{借金|しゃっきん}を{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}す (to default on a debt)
・{家賃|やちん}を{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}す (to skip out on rent)
・{飲|の}み{代|だい}を{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}す (to dine and dash)
・ツケを{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}す (to skip out on a tab)

NUANCE: Sense 2 (defaulting on payment) is the more common usage in everyday conversation. It carries a strong negative connotation of dishonesty and irresponsibility.

RELATED ～{倒|たお}す COMPOUND VERBS:
・{蹴|け}り{倒|たお}す - to kick down
・{殴|なぐ}り{倒|たお}す - to knock down (with fists)
・{押|お}し{倒|たお}す - to push down
